turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it: my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
This morning. The zero went in on November 3, Hale, so you read his work after you'd already decided. Who decided, and what do those essays actually show?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't told me who entered that zero or why, and I'm not here to talk about bedtime stories.
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here? A thoughtful kid has a zero sitting in your gradebook, and twenty minutes ago I'd have said you were the one who put it there.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It's a fight because you entered the zero before you picked up the phone, Hale. Show me something with a date on it, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
